post.caption: Amazonite's namesake river has no amazonite. Brazil does mine amazonite, in states such as Minas Gerais. Its blue green color mainly comes from lead and water in feldspar. For years, people guessed that copper made it green. Heat strips the color, yet radiation can restore it after mild heating. Egyptians made amazonite beads and amulets over 3,000 years ago. Carvers made tiny amazonite amulets, some under two centimeters across. Russia's Ilmen Mountains in the southern Urals are a historic source. Colorado's Crystal Peak area grows blue amazonite beside black smoky quartz. Virginia's Morefield Mine is considered the best American source.
